features: THE PADLOCK ONLY OPENED ON THE SERVER — Beta.33 moved the balance lock threshold from «an instalment plan exists» to «the plan is issued or collected». The engine learned it, with twenty-five tests to guarantee it. The interface did not: between creating a plan and issuing it, the server accepted corrections to an opening balance while the panel showed the padlock. No migration, and no data changes.

THE CASE THAT CAUSED BETA.32, ACTUALLY CLOSED. The padlock dialog advises «cancel the issue and the balance becomes editable again, without deleting the plan»: the advice was right and the system honoured it, but only behind the scenes — the icon stayed shut. The administrator followed an instruction printed inside the application, got nothing, and was left with one option: delete the plan. That is the exact path of the report beta.32 was born from, surviving the fix because nobody had looked at it with a mouse.

WHAT CHANGES ON SCREEN: balances of a plan that has not been issued have their pencil and bin back. The padlock appears when the plan is issued or has collections recorded, that is when the instalments are genuinely in the owners' hands.

THERE IS A NOTICE THAT WAS NOT NEEDED BEFORE. If a plan has already absorbed those balances but has not issued them, the panel says so: they are editable, but afterwards «Recalculate» must be pressed on the plan, because the instalments already generated stay as they were. It only appears on the management periods actually in that state: a notice that is always there is a notice people learn to ignore.
ORPHAN PADLOCKS STAY SHUT. Supplier debts and balances locked before beta.32 have no plan to trace back to: for them the lock remains, and they are reopened by hand as before.

Under the hood: the computed lock now travels in the payload alongside the raw one, and the server computes it once per plan — the predicate runs two queries, and calling it per row would mean two queries per balance on a page showing dozens. Removed a dead computation from beta.33, the per-management lock that no part of the interface read any more: removed rather than fixed, because a plausible name is what someone would call in good faith. The balances panel now has its first test: without one, the divergence between interface and engine was invisible to the suite by construction, which is how this defect survived eleven betas. Ten new tests, five per side.
